question: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and $\vec{b}=\hat{j}+\hat{k}$. Determine the vector $\vec{x}$ whose scalar products with $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$ are $3$, $4$ and $4$, respectively, and verify all three given conditions.
explanation: Formation of the Component EquationsLet`\vec{x}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}`The first scalar product condition gives`\vec{x}\cdot\vec{a}=3x+y=3`The second condition gives`\vec{x}\cdot\vec{b}=4y+z=4`Now,\\vec{a}\\times\\vec{b}=\\begin{vmatrix}\\hat{i} & \\hat{j} & \\hat{k}\\\\1 & 1 & 0\\\\0 & 1 & 1\\end{vmatrix}=\\hat{i}-\\hat{j}+\\hat{k}The third condition therefore gives`\vec{x}\cdot(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})=4x-y+z=4`Solving the EquationsFrom $x+y=3$ and $y+z=4$,`x=3-y,\qquad z=4-y`Substituting in $x-y+z=4$,`3-y-y+4-y=47-3y=4y=1`Therefore,`x=2,\qquad z=3`Hence,`\vec{x}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}`Verification`\vec{x}\cdot\vec{a}=(2)(1)+(1)(1)+(3)(0)=3\vec{x}\cdot\vec{b}=(2)(0)+(1)(1)+(3)(1)=4\vec{x}\cdot(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})=(2)(1)+(1)(-1)+(3)(1)=4`Final ResultThe required vector is $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$.
